0.value:
cv_image reads a picture from a file and sends it.

IT READS WHEN THE PATH ARRIVES:
Send a path to 'path in' - or type one into it - and the file is read and sent
straight away. A path given as the node's argument (cv_image <path>) is read
when the node is made. 'show image' sends the picture already read again; it does not go back to the file.

So the node is not watching the file. To pick up a changed file, send the path again. To walk through a directory, have something else supply one path after another.

A path that cannot be read prints a message in the console, and the picture read before it is dropped: 'show image' then sends nothing until a good path arrives.

THE ARRAY IS HEIGHT, WIDTH, CHANNELS - IN RGB:
The picture comes out as (height, width, 3) bytes, rows first, whatever the file held - an alpha channel is dropped and a grey image is made three-channel.

OpenCV reads files in blue, green, red order; cv_image converts to RGB before sending, like cv_camera and movie_player, so the pictures from all three can go to the same places. If you hand the array to an OpenCV function yourself, it will expect BGR and you will have to convert back.

SYNTAX:
cv_image <path>

EXAMPLE:
cv_image

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:

show image:
Anything at all sends the picture again.

path in:
The file. Receiving it reads the file and sends the picture.

OUTPUTS:

The single outlet carries the picture, as an RGB array of height by width by 3.

RELATED:
cv_camera for live pictures; cv_image used to share its page. movie_player for video files.
k. and tv. nodes for filtering and adjusting the image.
